subject: physics
title: The National Grid
key_idea: The National Grid links power stations to consumers. Step-up transformers raise the potential difference for transmission, which lowers the current and so reduces energy lost as heat in the cables. Step-down transformers lower it for homes.

blocks.text: The National Grid is a system of cables and transformers linking power stations to consumers. Electrical power is transferred from power stations to consumers through it.

items.meaning: A system of cables and transformers linking power stations to consumers.
A transformer that increases the potential difference.
A transformer that decreases the potential difference.

rows: Increases the potential difference for transmission.
Transmit the power over long distances.
Decrease it, to a much lower value, in each locality.

items: Electrical power is transferred at a high potential difference from power stations.
Step-up transformers increase the p.d. for transmission. Step-down transformers decrease it for domestic use.

sections.heading: Why a high potential difference is efficient

blocks.text: Cables have resistance, so some energy is transferred to the surroundings as heat. A high potential difference reduces this loss.

blocks.label: Power from potential difference and current
blocks.formula: power = potential difference × current    (P = V I)
where: potential difference, V, in volts, V

blocks.label: Power lost in a cable
where: power lost, P, in watts, W
resistance of the cable, R, in ohms, Ω

items.text: A step-up transformer increases V for transmission.
For the same power, P = V I means a larger V gives a smaller I.
Power lost is I²R, so a small current means much less thermal energy is transferred to the surroundings.
Less energy is wasted, so the transmission is more efficient.

diagram.alt: Choose the transmission potential difference and the power sent to see the current and the power lost in the cables.

outputs.label: Current in the cables, I = P / V
Power lost, I² × R (cable resistance 2 Ω)

blocks.text: Increase the potential difference 16 times and the current falls 16 times. The power lost, which depends on the current squared, falls far more.
Never say that a high potential difference means no energy is lost. It means less energy is lost.

blocks.label: Power in a transformer
blocks.formula: potential difference across primary coil × current in primary coil = potential difference across secondary coil × current in secondary coil    (Vp Ip = Vs Is)
where: Vp and Vs, in volts, V
Ip and Is, in amperes, A

blocks.text: The power out equals the power in. If a step-up transformer raises the p.d. 16 times, the current in the secondary coil falls 16 times.

diagram.alt: Calculate the current in the secondary coil of a step-down transformer using Vp x Ip = Vs x Is.
diagram.question: (Higher tier) The potential difference across the primary coil is {Vp} V and the current in it is {Ip} A. The potential difference across the secondary coil is {Vs} V. Calculate the current in the secondary coil.

items: High p.d. means low current for the same power.
Power lost in the cables is I²R, so a low current means much less heating.
Less energy is wasted, not none, so the transmission is more efficient.

checks.q: What is the job of a step-up transformer in the National Grid?
checks.a: It increases the potential difference from the power station to the transmission cables.

checks.q: Explain why electricity is transmitted at a very high potential difference.
checks.a: A very high potential difference means a very low current. Less thermal energy is transferred to the surroundings, which increases the efficiency of power transmission.

checks.q: What does a step-down transformer do, and where is one used?
checks.a: It decreases the potential difference to a much lower value, for domestic use in each locality.

exam_phrases: (very high p.d. means) very low currents
less (thermal) energy is transferred to surroundings
which increases the efficiency of power transmission
less heating in the transmission cables

mistakes.wrong: Step-up transformers make the network efficient because there is no energy loss.
mistakes.right: Do not say there is no energy loss. Say there is less energy loss to the surroundings.

mistakes.wrong: The step-up transformer increases the current and decreases the potential difference.
mistakes.right: A step-up transformer increases the potential difference and decreases the current, in that order.

mistakes.wrong: Step-up transformers reduce the resistance of the cables.
mistakes.right: Resistance is ignored in this explanation. The current is reduced, so there is less heating in the transmission cables.

worked_example.question: A network of transformers and transmission cables transfers electrical power from power stations to consumers. Explain how using step-up transformers makes the network efficient.
answer_points: So there is less energy loss to the surroundings (less heating in the transmission cables).
worked_example.tip: One mark each. Say less energy loss, never no energy loss.

exam_phrases: transformers are used to step up to a high voltage for transmission

mistakes.wrong: The National Grid uses high voltages with large currents.
mistakes.right: It uses high voltages with small currents. A small current reduces the heating effect in the cables.

mistakes.wrong: High voltages stop energy being lost in the cables.
mistakes.right: Say that heat loss is reduced, or that less energy or power is wasted in the cables.

mistakes.wrong: Power loss is I²R, so power loss is small.
mistakes.right: Link both equations. Vp Ip = Vs Is shows that a high voltage means a low current, and then P = I²R shows that the power loss is small.

worked_example.question: Explain why the National Grid uses high voltages with small currents to transfer electricity from power stations.
answer_points: Smaller currents reduce the heating effect in the cables.
So less energy or power is wasted in the cables, which increases efficiency.
worked_example.tip: Link any two points. Thermal energy is accepted for heat energy, and 'reduces heat energy loss' scores both marks.

exam_phrases: less energy wasted / lost / less heat in power lines
energy is transferred from the mains / via national grid / via transformers / via power lines

mistakes.wrong: High voltage stops energy being lost.
mistakes.right: Stops power loss and no energy wasted are not allowed. Say less energy is lost, or less heat in the power lines.

mistakes.wrong: It makes the National Grid more efficient.
mistakes.right: Ideas about efficiency alone are ignored. Say that the current decreases, so less energy is lost as heat in the power lines.

mistakes.wrong: A transformer that decreases 230 V to 12.1 V is a step-up transformer.
mistakes.right: It decreases the potential difference, so it is a step-down transformer. The transformer between a power station and the power lines is step-up.

worked_example.question: Explain why step-up transformers are used in the national grid.
answer_points: Transformers increase the voltage or potential difference (before the national grid).
Transformers decrease power or energy losses.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the three points. Do not write that energy losses stop completely.
